item.description:
Answer your agents wherever they run. This update finishes AgentDock's roadmap:

  • Answer Claude Code anywhere. With Settings › Agents outside cmux › *Know when Claude Code needs you* on, Claude's questions and permission prompts show up in the Inbox and are answered from there (allow, deny, or pick an answer), in any terminal and in the Claude app. Claude's own dialog stays up too; whichever you answer first wins.
  • Type into more terminals. Answers and replies now also reach agents in tmux, iTerm, WezTerm and kitty, not only cmux. (macOS asks once before AgentDock may control iTerm.)
  • herdr. Every agent herdr recognises in its panes (Claude, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode…) shows up and is answered through herdr.
  • Recaps and next steps. Finished cards get a one-line recap and three follow-ups to send with ⌘1–⌘3, written on this Mac by Apple Intelligence.
  • From your iPhone. Settings › iPhone serves a page your iPhone opens on the same Wi-Fi: scan the QR code, add it to the Home Screen, and answer from the couch. Off until you turn it on.
  • Codex approvals. An optional Codex hook marks approvals as needing you.

Claude Code everywhere, nothing to install. Every Claude Code session running outside cmux now shows up on the strip, in any terminal and in the Claude app, including sessions that were already running, with their own names and turn timers.

  • To also see when one of them needs you (a question or permission prompt), turn on Settings › Agents outside cmux › Know when Claude Code needs you. It adds a small hook to ~/.claude/settings.json and applies to sessions started afterwards.
  • Codex app and Codex CLI sessions show up as before.

Agents outside cmux. AgentDock now also shows the agents you run elsewhere:

  • Codex app and Codex CLI: threads from the Codex app (in ChatGPT) and the Codex CLI in any terminal appear on the strip with their names, turn timers and questions. Nothing to install; turn it off in Settings › Agents outside cmux.
  • Claude Code anywhere: turn on Settings › Agents outside cmux › Claude Code, and sessions in any terminal, the Claude app and your editor show up too. This adds a small hook to ~/.claude/settings.json (backed up first); turning it off removes it.
  • Clicking one takes you there: the right iTerm or Terminal tab, tmux pane, or the app it runs in. The Inbox lists them too; answering them from AgentDock comes in a later update (for now ↩ opens them).

Also faster: reading long Codex sessions no longer slows down on very large log lines.
